liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Cold Rain And Snow** (1 review): Reviewer calls the opening Cold Rain And Snow blazing, setting the tone for the show [10]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Reviewer doubts the LP matches because of how China Cat jams out at its end into I Know You Rider [8]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 other source): Uploader notes odd edits and patchwork in this audience tape's I Know You Rider [7]
- **I'm A King Bee** (1 review): Reviewer hears Pigpen in rare form on King Bee and on Lovelight [10]

## Setlist highlights

- **The Rub**: rare: 12 archived performances [20]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Sing Me Back Home [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-04-05.sbd.miller.110127.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 182 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd1971-04-05.sbd.cantor.gmb.96269.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 174 min; rated 4.71/5 by 7 [2]
- **gd1971-04-05.sbd.orf.117.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 168 min; rated 4.8/5 by 5 [5]
- **gd71-04-05.sbd.ladner.12367.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 165 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer thinks this Ladner soundboard taping is as good as, or better than, the other recording of the show [17]
- **gd1971-04-05.partial.aud.berger.100052.flac16**: audience recording; 16 songs; 91 min [7]. Said about its sound: Audience partial: most songs lose their first notes, and loud passages get severely clipped, suggesting automatic level control or a limiter [7]

## Around the show

- Listing names NRPS as another artist involved, and labels the Lovelight segment a 'Dance Marathon' [1]
- Reviewer says the cuts on the underground LP "Ain't It Crazy", opening with The Rub, are supposedly from this concert and sound very similar [8]
- Reviewer ranks the second set among the best of 1971, with Pigpen and Garcia standing out [9]
- Reviewer says the Truckin' into The Other One medley carries the intensity and color of 1969 performances [10]
- Reviewer finds this Not Fade Away is not the Skull & Roses one; Garcia's and Weir's vocals differ [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-04-05.sbd.miller.110127.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat (44.1k) [1]
- **gd1971-04-05.sbd.cantor.gmb.96269.flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by Bill Koucky; source: 7" two track reel @ 7 1/2 ips > PCM501ES (beta) PCM501ES analog out > dolby A decoder > analog in PCMF1 > analog out > Fostex D5 Dat @ 48 kHz [2]. Also: Two cuts remain in The Other One and Lovelight, edited by removing tape squeeze and smoothing with minor fades; Dropouts at reel changes were removed and crossfaded, including before Me & Bobby McGee, Loser, China Cat Sunflower and Sugar Magnolia [2]
- **gd1971-04-05.sbd.orf.117.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Leigh Orf [5]. Also: Leigh Orf digitally remastered the original wav files, removing a tone around 7-8 kHz and smoothing reel flips [5]
- **gd71-04-05.sbd.ladner.12367.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Leigh Orf and Chris Ladner; source: Soundboard [6]
- **gd1971-04-05.partial.aud.berger.100052.flac16**: transferred by Rob Berger; source: aud of unknown origin lineage [7]. Also: The Other One is intact on this audience tape and could patch the two cuts in the soundboard [7]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Pandora: [Not Fade Away / Goin' down the Road Feeling Bad (Live at Manhattan Center, New York, NY, April 5, 1971)](https://www.pandora.com/artist/grateful-dead/grateful-dead-skull-and-roses-live/not-fade-away-goin-down-the-road-feeling-bad-live-at-manhattan-center-new-york-ny-april-5-1971/TR3KzvJtpk4Jvg4) [21]
